purpose.summary: Visual indicator for a transient, system-driven state. Uses a closed, evaluative semantic palette (muted/success/warning/danger/info/merged/risk), never an open categorical one. See status-badge.guide.md SBD-001/002 for when to choose StatusBadge vs Tag.
useWhen: Value is a state that changes automatically (pending → active → closed).
Exactly one status per object (mutually exclusive).
Status can change while visible; caller wraps with aria-live=polite.
doNotUseWhen: Value is a stable attribute describing what a thing is — use Tag instead.
Multiple statuses apply to the same object — show one badge with the most urgent status (EXS-001).
Badge needs to be interactive — use Tag's interactive props.
Need open/uncontrolled color palette — use Tag's 15-color palette.
Need to combine two statuses (e.g. 'Error, Pending') — pick the most urgent. Don't render a second badge (EXS-001).

accessibility.notes: Non-interactive by design: role, aria-readonly, tabIndex, onClick and color are omitted from props. All semantic meaning lives in children text. No built-in aria-live; callers must wrap with aria-live=polite for live-changing status. See EXS-003 in the execution-status pattern.

governance.note: Pattern decisions (StatusBadge vs Tag), accessibility gaps, pipeline-icon conventions: see SBD-001 through SBD-018 in the guide, less the four retired in favor of the execution-status pattern. Most rules are 'proposed' or 'open'. Treat them as context until ratified.
governance.tokenStatus: All refs exist in packages/core-design-system/design-tokens (validator check, 2026-10-20). Refs cover the primary variant colors only. See knownGaps.

knownGaps.summary: Docs list variant as optional with default 'primary'; StatusBadgeProps requires it.
Icon renders in a fixed DOM order with no RTL logic.
pulse applies animate-pulse with no prefers-reduced-motion guard.
knownGaps.source: status-badge.tsx indicator span; 'reduced-motion' appears only in stepper code

knownGaps.summary: pulse has no Figma property; it is a code-only animation.
Contract requires children (SBD-006) but StatusBadgeProps inherits an optional children from React.HTMLAttributes, so an icon-only or empty badge type-checks.
Code Connect reads 'text#1299:25' and 'icon#1293:13'. Figma reports the keys as 'textString#1299:25' and 'viewIcon#1293:13'. The manifest uses the Figma keys; status-badge.figma.ts is unchanged.
Figma defines state=hover for primary, secondary and outline. Code has no hover styles for .cn-badge, and the component is non-interactive (SBD-004).
Figma md variants bind badge/sm/gap, badge/sm/px and badge/sm/py (gap 2px, px 6px, py 2px). Code md uses badge.md.* (gap 4px, px 8px, py 4px).
knownGaps.source: Figma boundVariables on 1293:5995 variants (2026-10-20) vs badge.ts .cn-badge and badge.json

knownGaps.summary: Figma status variant has 0 padding. Code applies the .cn-badge md/sm padding to the status variant (only ghost resets padding).
tokens.refs list primary-variant colors only. Code also reads set.<theme>.secondary.*, set.<theme>.outline.bg/border and text.1 (status text).
The outline variant has no text token in the token source; code uses set.<theme>.secondary.text for outline and ghost text.
knownGaps.source: badge.ts lines 28-46; mode/light/default.json set.*.outline has bg, bg-hover, bg-selected, border
